the session transcript independent of hookSpecificOutput -- the
channel the operator actually reads. A spawn with no persona and no
verifier isolation block previously emitted no JSON at all when there
was nothing else to say; it now still emits one carrying just the
diagnostic. Stderr keeps carrying the same text for forensics.

Tests assert the diagnostic reaches additionalContext and
SystemMessage for both the match case and the degraded-uncertainty
case, is absent from SystemMessage in the quiet cases, and a new
regression (TestSubagentStart_LoudSkipDiagnosticEmittedWithNoPersona)
covers the persona-absent gap directly, using a mission-store
identity distinct from the session's persona-resolution store so
matched=true and persona=="" hold simultaneously.

Live verification -- a real spawn showing the message to the operator
-- is a leader-side Phase 3 step before merge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF

tool_input.message:
Re-verification result: items 1-5 and 7-9 verified; item 6 verified with one exception; the fresh sweep found one substantive adversarial issue in the item-5 fix and two minor issues. go test -race passes for both packages.

Per-item:

1. VERIFIED (9e2b8b5). isEvaluatorOfOpenMission (internal/hook/subagent_start.go:791-815) warns to stderr on the List error (line 794) and on each skipped Load (line 803), and returns hadError. The doc comment (lines 786-790) now states the asymmetry with checkWriteSetConflicts explicitly instead of claiming parity; I confirmed checkWriteSetConflicts (internal/mission/store.go:3170) warns but does not report the fault back, so the new wording is accurate.

2. VERIFIED (816b1f8). The three-outcome switch is at subagent_start.go:688-699: matched emits the loud-skip diagnostic, hadError-without-match emits the "cannot determine whether" uncertainty diagnostic, clean no-match stays quiet. The corrupt-matching-mission test exists: TestSubagentStart_LoudSkipUncertaintyDiagnosticWhenMatchingMissionFailsToLoad (subagent_start_test.go:1169) plus TestIsEvaluatorOfOpenMission_ListErrorWarnsAndSuppresses (1100) and the surviving-match test (1129).

3. VERIFIED (d545887). SubagentStartResult.SystemMessage exists (subagent_start.go:46) with a doc comment explaining stderr is deployment-silent; I confirmed plugin/hooks/subagent-start.sh line 8 redirects stderr to ~/.punt-labs/ethos/hook-errors.log, so the claim is accurate. The diagnostic is prepended to additionalContext (lines 230-235), the no-persona path still emits JSON when a diagnostic exists (lines 263-271, tested at subagent_start_test.go:997), and two tests assert all three channels in a loop over {stderr, additionalContext, SystemMessage} (lines 969-984 and 1196-1208).

4. VERIFIED (faaf49f). isDriveLetterPrefix (internal/mission/conflict.go:574-581) requires exactly one ASCII letter plus ':'. splitSegments consults it at line 556. The **/notes.go vs C:/anything/notes.go test exists (conflict_test.go:635-636), alongside backslash, bare-drive-letter, and positive drive-letter-entry cases (620-652).

5. VERIFIED (3a75dcb), with adversarial findings below. pathAllowed (internal/hook/pretooluse.go:322-340) uses filepath.Rel with ".."-prefix rejection (line 326) and tries both the raw and repo-relative forms (lines 332, 335). repoRoot is threaded from one envRepoRoot() call (line 125) to both pathAllowed call sites (lines 127 and 139).

Adversarial analysis of the dual-try:
(a) SUBSTANTIVE (MEDIUM): the repo-relative branch trusts envRepoRoot, whose fallback is bare os.Getwd() with no repo-marker validation (tierBRepoRoot, internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go:1052-1067 - raw cwd, not git-root discovery). With ETHOS_REPO_ROOT unset and the hook cwd not the repo root, an absolute target under cwd is resolved as repo-relative against the wrong base: cwd=/repo/internal with target /repo/internal/docs/x.md yields relTarget "docs/x.md", which entry "docs/**" admits even though the contract meant repo-root docs/. Pre-fix code denied every such target (absolute segments never matched a relative entry), so this is a genuine admit-widening introduced by the fix, gated on a wrong repoRoot. Likelihood is low (Claude Code runs hooks at the project root and Tier B sets ETHOS_REPO_ROOT), but the fallback should be git-root discovery or should refuse relTarget resolution when the root lacks a repo marker.
(b) MINOR: strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..") also rejects a legal in-repo filename beginning with "..", e.g. /repo/..config yields rel "..config" and is dropped, producing a false deny. Loud (deny names the path), not silent. Standard idiom: rel != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, "../").
(c) repoRoot "/" makes every absolute path repo-relative; that is semantically consistent when the repo root genuinely is "/", so not a defect, but it compounds (a) if ETHOS_REPO_ROOT were ever set to "/".
(d) Symlinks and lexical-".."-cleaning can still land a lexically-admitted write outside the repo; pre-existing, and documented as "write_set is not a sandbox" (DES-069). A relative target that names a different file than its repo-relative reading is also pre-existing raw-compare behavior, not added by the dual-try.

6. VERIFIED WITH ONE EXCEPTION (1a82a12). H1, H3, H4, H5 all route through writeSetContains -> PathContainedBy (lint.go:187-194); writeSetIndex is gone (grep confirms zero references); regression tests exist for each converted heuristic plus the ethos-vaib absolute-input case. Exception: lintChangelog (H2, internal/mission/lint.go:90-98) still decides CHANGELOG coverage by literal canonical-string comparison (cp == "CHANGELOG.md" || cp == "changelog.md"). A write_set of ["internal/foo.go", "*.md"] draws the "production code but no CHANGELOG.md" advisory even though "*.md" covers CHANGELOG.md - the exact defect class of ethos-8ady, and "*.md" is a legal entry (the new H3 test uses it). The fix is writeSetContains(c.WriteSet, "CHANGELOG.md") || writeSetContains(c.WriteSet, "changelog.md"). Secondary, same family but different shape: isWriteSetPrefix (lint.go:278-291) treats glob entries as literal text, so write_set ["internal/**"] with context mentioning "internal/mission" draws a spurious H7 cross-repo warning. Both are advisory-only (info/warn, non-blocking).

7. VERIFIED (a961aa0). None of the formerly-false strings ("carries no", "will persist", "873--932", "no such guard", "does not refuse a") remain in docs/spec-mission-lifecycle.tex. The replacement text's code claims are accurate: Store.Update's on-disk terminal guard exists at internal/mission/store.go:914-916 (checks onDisk.Status, not the caller's), and TestStore_Update_CannotReopenClosedMission is at store_test.go:4279 exactly as cited. The remaining stOpen-to-terminal gap (ethos-w1ii) is real: Update's body calls neither checkResultGateLocked nor countBlockingDelegations.

8. VERIFIED. The widening Implementation note exists at docs/spec-writeset-admission.tex:435 ("Implementation note: the allowlist's one absolute entry"), directly after PathContainedByFixed in the containment section. Its cited pins check out: conflict_test.go:599 is "an absolute file IS contained by a matching absolute entry" and pretooluse_test.go ~455 is the absolute-match row. Two of its code citations have drifted a few lines (pathContainedBy is now at conflict.go:388, not 367-410; verifierAllowlistSplit is now at subagent_start.go:494, not 457-489) - cosmetic, from later commits on the same branch.

9. VERIFIED. go test -race ./internal/hook/... ./internal/mission/... : both packages ok (hook 3.7s, mission 5.8s), zero failures.

Fresh sweep of 9052b9e..HEAD -- internal/ for new silent failures: the new stderr warnings added by 9e2b8b5 are not silent overall because the session-visible SystemMessage/additionalContext channel carries the resulting diagnostic; the extract_into stat-error path falls through to a loud deny; overlapSegments discarding the absoluteness flag is justified by validator guarantees and documented in place. New findings are limited to 5(a), 5(b), and the item-6 lintChangelog exception above. Zero other new silent failures.

Two findings from the re-verification of 3a75dcb; fix in internal/hook/pretooluse.go (+ pretooluse_test.go, and pretooluse_dispatch.go if the fallback lives there); make check green; commit; report hash.

1. MEDIUM — the repo-relative branch trusts envRepoRoot, whose fallback is bare os.Getwd() with no repo-marker validation (tierBRepoRoot, internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go:1052-1067). With ETHOS_REPO_ROOT unset and hook cwd not the repo root (e.g. cwd=/repo/internal, target /repo/internal/docs/x.md), relTarget resolves against the wrong base and "docs/**" admits a file the contract never meant — an admit-widening the fix introduced, since pre-fix such targets were always denied. Fix: before using the fallback root for relTarget resolution, validate it carries a repo marker (.git or .punt-labs/ethos — pick the marker the surrounding hook code already uses, check resolve package helpers first for an existing git-root discovery to reuse rather than writing a new one); when the root cannot be validated, skip the repo-relative try (keep the raw try), restoring pre-fix behavior rather than widening. Test: cwd-not-root simulation → target not admitted via the wrong-base resolution.

2. MINOR — strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..") also rejects a legal in-repo name starting with ".." (e.g. /repo/..config → rel "..config" → false deny). Standard idiom: rel != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, "../"). Test row for a "..-prefixed" in-repo filename.

Then stop and report.
